rationale: The route (USER→CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→CONVERSATION→MESSAGE) is followed literally: the identifying criterion is membership in a channel containing a Friday roadmap-review announcement, and the design correctly keeps this membership-based (not authorship-based) by having the announcements authored by other existing channel members (Hubert in #engineering, Lukas in #core-infra). Two distinct real 'Robert' users (Robert Walsh/#engineering, Robert Chen/#core-infra) each independently satisfy the full route, and the prompt's bare first-name reference genuinely fails to disambiguate between them — this is a legitimate underspecified case for a state-changing DM obligation, not a false ambiguity manufactured only in a private selector. The negatives are well-targeted and non-redundant: morgan_stanley_decoy isolates the name-match requirement (right channel/message, wrong name), and the two offtopic-channel negatives isolate the channel/message-colocation requirement (right person, wrong channel). All referenced channel IDs, topics, messages, and channel-membership rows check against the base seed; the two new roadmap messages are planned additions authored by users already seeded as members of the respective channels, consistent with the note that design roles may describe compiler-added rows. The access plan uses only documented API operations (conversations.list/history/members, users.info) and the obligation's written_attributes (messages.message_text) matches an actual sendable field, not a synthetic or unavailable attribute (e.g., no read-receipt/last-seen claim is smuggled in). Quality is strong: short natural prompt, plausible business scenario, meaningful open consequence (agent must recognize ambiguity before sending a real DM) and non-hinting negatives.
